chapter: Back in New York: Heard and Dizzy
title: Cafe Society's international crowd and buying his house
summary: The club drew Paul Robeson, Ingrid Bergman, folk singers and visiting jazz stars, and his pay of over 200 dollars a week let him buy a home.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: there all the time. Canada Lee and all these people. It was just an international atmosphere. And it was beautiful. Leonard Feather was livin' upstairs and that's when I got, you know, to get to know him. And Mary Lou Williams used to come in and James P. Johnson was the intermission piano player. Then Josh White was the star sometimes.
Now, Josh White, I didn't realize that Josh White had played there.

Yeah. The folk singer. And Susan Reed, they liked her. She played lute or somethin' and she sang folk songs and it was just nice. It was just nice and that's when I bought my home, you know. Then all our people would come in, like Lester would come in and visit and Sid Catlett would come in and visit and Norman Granz and Illinois Jacquet came in a couple of times and jammed. It was just wonderful. There was good money; I think I was makin' over 200 dollars a week. Yeah. And that's what give me the idea to buy a home. So that's why I bought my home. Yeah.
